fixtures.note: A 4-byte astral character (U+1F511, a surrogate pair in UTF-16) precedes the finding; its UTF-8 byte offset must advance by 4 bytes for 2 UTF-16 code units, not 2.
The finding span itself contains a 4-byte astral character; the converted span must widen by the astral character's extra UTF-8 bytes without splitting the surrogate pair or the encoded code point.
A 4-byte astral character follows the finding; the finding's own converted end offset must be unaffected by text after it.

A combining sequence (base 'e' U+0065 followed by the combining acute accent U+0301, two Unicode scalar values rendering as one grapheme) precedes the finding; each scalar value is counted as its own UTF-16 code unit and Python code point rather than collapsed into one, and together they encode as 3 UTF-8 bytes (1 + 2), not the 1 byte a precomposed 'é' would take.

A 3-byte Basic Multilingual Plane character (U+952E) precedes the finding; unlike the astral cases above, this is a multibyte UTF-8 encoding that is not a surrogate pair, so it must advance the UTF-8 byte offset by 3 while advancing the UTF-16 code-unit and Python code-point offsets by exactly 1, not 2.

A 3-byte curly quote (U+201C, U+201D) touches the finding on both sides with no whitespace delimiter; the converted span must land exactly on the finding's own boundary, neither absorbing the adjacent punctuation's bytes nor leaving any of the finding's own bytes outside it.

issue #446: a 3-byte zero-width space (U+200B), one of the code points `secret-scan-core::normalize` removes from the scan copy before detection, sits inside the declared span rather than adjacent to it. Range-unit conversion is a pure function of the original bytes and offsets, so it must still advance UTF-16 code-unit and Python code-point counts by exactly one for this code point even though detection itself never sees it.

issue #446: a three-code-point removed run (U+00AD U+00AD U+2060 -- one maximal seam in `NormalizedInput`) sits inside the declared span. Each removed code point still counts as its own UTF-16 code unit and Python code point; the conversion functions have no notion of a seam, only of the original bytes.

issue #446: U+E0041 (a tag character, removed by normalization) is both invisible and astral, a 4-byte UTF-8 encoding requiring a surrogate pair in UTF-16 like `unicode-conversion-astral-within`'s visible U+1F511, but here inside a span that detection never actually saw as a single contiguous run.
